messages:
claire: Heads-up: our integration tests are flaky on CI with uvloop enabled. sometimes tests blow up with "RuntimeError: Event loop is closed" coming from the SDK client teardown.

tom: can you paste the failing trace? is this during pytest worker shutdown?

claire: short trace: Task exception was never retrieved
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
  File "/workspace/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_async/client.py", line 120, in aclose
    await self._transport.aclose()

It seems the client's background keepalive tries to close after loop already closed. We use a module-scoped fixture that creates the client once.

yuki: are you using pytest-asyncio and uvloop together? pytest-asyncio sets up its own loop policy and uvloop installs a policy; double-check fixture scope and how the client is created.

claire: repro in tests:
```py
# conftest.py
import pytest
from redwood import AsyncClient

@py.test.fixture(scope='module')
def client():
    return AsyncClient()  # created outside any running loop
```
then multiple async test functions call `await client.generate(...)`. Locally usually fine, on CI sometimes the loop is closed by pytest shutdown race.

tom: creating client outside running loop is risky. We should either: 1) change fixture to async def + create inside the running loop (async with AsyncClient()), or 2) make AsyncClient lazy-start background tasks.

claire: switching to async fixture fixes it in our suite but wanted to flag for SDK: many customers use module-level fixtures or import-time clients.

yuki: agreed. SDK action items: - document recommended fixture patterns, - implement lazy-start (start tasks on first await), - make aclose/idempotent and tolerant if loop is closing.

test-bot: created issue #712: "pytest/uvloop: client teardown race when created outside running loop" and linked failing CI job: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/2345

sara: small patch idea: in AsyncClient.__del__ and aclose catch RuntimeError('Event loop is closed') and suppress with a debug log suggesting explicit close. also make __init__ not spawn tasks unless `asyncio.get_running_loop()` succeeds.

yuki: downside: silently suppressing errors can hide real leaks. prefer explicit warnings at delete-time and a runtime debug flag to raise on improper usage. add a clear FAQ blurb.

claire: for our tests I pushed a quick fix: change fixture to async and ensure client closed:
```py
@pytest.fixture(scope='module')
async def client():
    async with AsyncClient() as c:
        yield c
```
CI pipeline green after that. I'll attach the test diff to the issue.

tom: can we add a small integration test in sdk repo that runs under uvloop and creates client at import time then runs two asyncio.run() cycles in subprocess to catch regressions? would prevent this regressing.

yuki: yes — add a tiny subprocess-based test that uses `python -c "..."` to avoid pytest loop internals. I'll open a PR after the issue triage.

claire: thanks all. marking this thread resolved once PR lands. closing notes: doc update, lazy-init PR, and test coverage for uvloop. :white_check_mark:
